entries.name: Capybara
entries.definition: A Ruby library for testing web applications by simulating how a user interacts with them.

entries.name: Cardiac stress testing
entries.definition: Conducting tests that record how the heart responds to physical exercise or to drugs that simulate exercise.

entries.name: Cardiac surgery
entries.definition: The surgical specialty that operates on the heart.

entries.name: Cardiac valve repair
entries.definition: Surgically reconstructing a damaged heart valve so that it works again without replacing it.

entries.name: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
entries.definition: An emergency procedure that combines chest compressions and rescue breaths to keep blood and oxygen moving when someone's heart or breathing has stopped.

entries.name: Cardiothoracic surgery
entries.definition: The surgical specialty that operates on organs in the chest, mainly the heart and lungs.

entries.name: Cardiovascular coding
entries.definition: Assigning standard diagnosis and procedure codes to heart and blood-vessel care records for billing and reporting.

entries.name: Cardiovascular physiology
entries.definition: The study of how the heart and blood vessels work.

entries.name: Care coordination
entries.definition: Organising a patient's care across providers and services so that the patient's needs are met.

entries.name: Carrot2
entries.definition: An open-source search results clustering engine that groups documents and search results into topics.

entries.name: CARTO
entries.definition: A cloud platform for analysing and mapping location data, formerly called CartoDB.

entries.name: Cartographic design
entries.definition: Designing maps so that geographic data is clear and readable, through choices of symbols, colour, labelling and scale.

entries.name: Case analysis
entries.definition: Examining the facts and issues of a particular case, such as a legal, business or clinical case, to reach reasoned conclusions or recommendations.

entries.name: Case method
entries.definition: A teaching approach in which students learn by studying and discussing real or realistic cases, common in business and law schools.

entries.name: CasperJS
entries.definition: An open-source tool, written in JavaScript, for scripting navigation and tests of web pages in headless browsers such as PhantomJS and SlimerJS.

entries.name: Casualty movement
entries.definition: Moving injured or ill people from where they were hurt to places where they can be treated, including loading and transporting them.

entries.name: CatBoost
entries.definition: An open-source gradient-boosting library, originally from Yandex, that trains decision-tree models and handles categorical features directly.

entries.name: CCH ProSystem fx Engagement
entries.definition: Wolters Kluwer CCH software that accounting firms use to manage engagements and workpapers.

entries.name: CDC Cyber
entries.definition: A line of mainframe and supercomputer systems made by Control Data Corporation from the 1970s.

entries.name: cebas finalRender
entries.definition: A rendering plug-in from cebas Visual Technology for producing photorealistic images in 3D software such as Autodesk 3ds Max and Maya.

entries.name: Celoxis
entries.definition: Web-based project and portfolio management software for planning work, tracking time and resources, and reporting on projects.

entries.name: CentiLeo
entries.definition: A GPU-based 3D renderer that produces images from 3D scenes, offered as a plug-in for 3D modelling software.

entries.name: Cerner
entries.definition: Electronic health record software from the company Cerner, now part of Oracle Health, that hospitals use to chart, order and review patient information.

entries.name: Ceros
entries.definition: A cloud platform for designing interactive online content such as ebooks, microsites and lookbooks without writing code.

entries.name: CFWheels
entries.definition: An open-source model-view-controller web framework for CFML (ColdFusion Markup Language).

entries.name: Chai.js
entries.definition: An assertion library for JavaScript testing that offers should, expect and assert styles.

entries.name: Chain Conveyor
entries.definition: A conveyor that moves loads along a track using one or more driven chains.

entries.name: Chain of custody
entries.definition: The documented, unbroken record of who held a piece of evidence or sample and when, used to show it was not altered.

entries.name: Chainer
entries.definition: An open-source Python deep learning framework from Preferred Networks that builds neural networks as the code runs.

entries.name: Challenge-Handshake Authentication Protocol
entries.definition: A challenge-response protocol, used with the Point-to-Point Protocol, that checks a peer's identity by hashing a shared secret with a random challenge.

entries.name: Change agility
entries.definition: The capacity to adapt quickly and effectively as circumstances and organisational priorities change.

entries.name: Change management planning
entries.definition: Planning how an organisation will move people through a change, including stakeholder engagement, communication and training.

entries.name: Changing oil
entries.definition: Draining the used engine oil from a vehicle or machine and refilling it with fresh oil, usually with a new filter.

entries.name: Channel sales
entries.definition: Selling products or services through partners such as resellers and distributors rather than directly to end customers.

entries.name: Character art
entries.definition: Designing and producing the visual appearance of characters for games, animation and film.

entries.name: Chart.js
entries.definition: An open-source JavaScript library for drawing charts on an HTML canvas.

entries.name: Chemical reactions
entries.definition: The processes by which substances change into other substances, and the types, rates and energy changes involved.

entries.name: Child and adolescent psychiatry
entries.definition: The medical specialty that diagnoses and treats mental, emotional and behavioural disorders in children and teenagers.

entries.name: Child nutrition
entries.definition: The nutritional needs of infants, children and adolescents and how diet meets them.

entries.name: Children's Health Insurance Program
entries.definition: The US federal and state programme that provides low-cost health coverage for children in families that earn too much for Medicaid.
